title: SPRAWL zero
description: SPRAWL zero is a fast-paced shooter inspired by the Golden Age of 2000s FPS. Survive a brutal cyberpunk city collapsing under military rule and cult fanaticism. Use your Gravity-Gloves, augments, and an arsenal of over 40 weapons to crush those who stand in your way.

conclusion.verdict: Общее впечатление блогера крайне положительное: игра признана одним из лучших опытов стрельбы в последнее время благодаря отличной динамике и атмосфере. Однако автор отмечает, что драйв порой омрачается техническими проблемами, однообразными задачами и неудачной реализацией финального босса.

segments.text: Well, I think it's safe to say we're finally getting away from the 90s boomer shooter throwbacks and moving ahead into the early 2000s with a perfect example here with Sprawl zero fast-paced and physics-driven shooter that feels like some kind of long-lost Xbox or PS2 era title

Along with it also taking heavy influence from games like Fear, Halo and Half-Life series As if all these games got together in a filthy cyberpunk themed bathroom and started doing amphetamines together Not really a boomer shooter, more like a millennial shooter from that brief period where FPS games were still fast and violent but developers had started filling them with physics systems, smarter enemies and all kinds of experimental mechanics Either way though, like whatever this thing is doing, it works and it's

almost become my favorite FPS for 2026. If it wasn't for some things at the back end that really kind of irritate me. But if all you want to know though is if this thing is worth picking up, then I can confidently say that yes. Yes it is. It's got some of the best shooting I've experienced in recent memory and it's just a really interesting and unique experience overall. Let's find out what it is, shall we?

Now Sprawl zero is a prequel taking place before the events in the first game where you're playing as this enhanced super soldier named five Accentation is to execute Working for the junta and trying to take down this hostile rebel faction called the Imago Dei and in particular their leader Silas A dude who looks like he took fashion advice from solidus snake with a head like skull of Asari from killzone With your first task being to just head into a nearby section of the city and wipe these guys out where it should become

Pretty obvious you're not really working for the good guys. The thing is, is that there's not really any good guys to be seen here, considering the Imago Dei ain't exactly Boy Scouts either. When you find out that they indoctrinate their recruits into murderous fanatics that just then follow their orders blindly. And their whole belief system is that technology is what's ruined humanity. So their plan is to wipe the slate clean and bring everyone back to a pre-industrial society.

in a nice touch too you don't actually end up working alongside the rebels i mean you'd think that the plot would be that about halfway into the game your character realizes he's taken orders from the bad guys and then swapped sides right but refreshingly it has none of that and both sides are bad for their own different reasons both needing to be wiped out visually it looks like what most cyberpunk themed games do where you're traveling through what's essentially a futuristic version of kowloon city

but credit where it's due like this thing really does look gorgeous and has totally captured the vibe of those Xbox and PS2 era titles from the early to mid 2000s with the enemies all wearing suitably badass looking armor and textures having just the right amount of filtering and a low resolution to capture that period in gaming really just encapsulating that feeling of walking around this vast futuristic cityscape where corruption has caused just about as many problems as overpopulation has

Not to mention it's got an insanely cool drum and bass soundtrack and I mean like what sort of 2000s inspired game would this be if it didn't have this There's some really nice atmospheric moments when it's raining and later on when you're moving through the destroyed remains of certain sections The city is eerily quiet with the color palette almost always being muted with lots of browns and greys Still though doing a pretty good job of mixing things up with one of the later areas looking like an MC Escher painting brought to life

There's a whole lot of neat visual effects in here as well. The kind of stuff that you totally see in an old early 2000s shooter. Like volumetric lighting, which has almost been placed in here, I think, ironically. It's kind of hard to explain what I mean by this, but there was always this kind of thing in older games where you'd enter an area and then see some kind of nifty new trick that the engine could pull off. Be it with the lighting, a reflection, or a water effect.

It's a bit of a dead art form these days considering that these effects are so commonplace that they're just not really impressive but back then you'd always see developers squeezing something like this into the level design if only just to show off some cool new tech where it always made you stop and drew your eyeline which is what it kind of feels like they've done here deliberately drawing your attention to a specific spot in the environment

the kind of thing that you really only get from hand-crafted more compact and focused environments and the kind of thing that's just utterly lost in most open-world games these days and that's the great thing about SPRAWL zero is that it's actually trying to recreate how developers designed games back then it's not just copying how those games looked it's copying how they thought

with one of the best examples of what to compare it to having to be the Half-Life series. I mean, for starters, all of Silas's little speeches throughout the city are very reminiscent of seeing Dr. Breen yapping on in City 17. The world itself has that whole oppressive thing going on too with huge industrial spaces, military occupation, propaganda, and the general feeling that the technology that was supposed to save humanity is instead what's made everything so bad off. Who am I to stop it?

The suit you wear is kinda similar to Gordon's HEV, even having a Geiger counter that clicks away when you're in radiated areas. With these gravity guvs just being essentially a gravity gun in the palm of your hand, able to pick up objects and throw them around, and even live grenades, which look and behave a lot like the Combine ones did in Half-Life 2. Oh yeah, and speaking of the Combine, the enemies all have a...

kind of similar look here as well along with an almost identical death sound with their screams turning into a flatline you encounter female assassins as well similar to those in half-life and frequently throughout the levels you're getting attacked by gunships that swoop around to shoot at you you want to get nuts let's get nuts how about near the end of the game your gravity gloves get an upgrade so they can outright pick enemies up and throw them around

The only difference is that for the finale in Half-Life 2, you were ascending to the Combine Citadel. Here though, you're descending beneath the city to take on this all new enemy faction. Oh yeah, and if this room here isn't a Ghost in the Shell reference, then I don't know what is. It has been attempting to boost the surface for some time. At its heart though, this is still just a shoot-up first and foremost, and a pretty damn good one at that too. With a high focus on speed and mobility, along with utilizing these primary abilities over and over.

with the main one being that gravity glove a super handy tool that can not only destroy most enemies with a single punch but also yank every single object like weapons or props straight into your hands which becomes a very useful mechanic even able to yank guns out of mid-air during combat without losing a beat you rarely hold on to a gun for more than 10 seconds here too simply because you only get ammunition for a single magazine and then after that about all it's good for is throwing at enemies

All of the weapons come in different tiers with the weak guns being less effective while the high tier stuff just shreds through enemies with there being some really effective guns here too to mess around with Like this gnarly minigun that just shreds through everything There's a nail gun that decimates most enemies in a single hit along with the thermal saw which is a giant melee weapon that pulverizes everything as well There's also a super powerful hand cannon which is absolutely a staple of older FPS games like Killzone

And then later on in the game you start coming across a katana that can even deflect bullets One of the best ones is a shotgun that lights enemies on fire which is so effective that it almost feels like a war crime And something that's actually a pretty recurring theme here too in just how brutal and effective these shotguns are I mean someone definitely got the memo when it came to making sure all of these are great to use

I don't even know how to fully describe some of them either I mean like this one I guess is also causing electrical damage It almost kind of reminds me of those old monolith production games like Shogo and Blood 2 where they just included a shitload of stupidly overpowered weapons so many to the point that you could potentially miss some of them if you didn't experiment and it's just this seemingly never-ending list of awesome guns to play with where just when you think you've seen all there is another one drops and you get to use it for the very first time

Combining all of this with 5's abilities, the bullet time, the gravity shield and then a melee ability called Rushdown With the game really not wasting time and giving you those first two Now bullet time is pretty self-explanatory and I'd wager that most people are gonna know how this thing works You activate it, everything slows down around you but you can still aim in real time The difference here though is that whenever this is activated all of the shots you fire are gonna home in on the nearest enemies

which in the case of weapons like the shotgun means every single pellet is gonna hit that poor bastard that's unlucky enough to be on the business end of those things resulting in some really satisfying and cathartic deaths and if you're not using bullet time constantly and in every single gunfight well then I'm sorry to tell you man but you're playing the game wrong and I swear too like just when I start to think that a feature like bullet time is getting a bit played out something like this comes along and I'm instantly hooked right back in

After that, you've got the gravity shield, which absorbs bullets that would otherwise hit you. And then after you've been exposed to more lead than a child in the 1950s, you can launch all of these back at every nearby enemy. Which is also another essential ability. Seeing as the combat's totally designed around this, given the often overwhelming odds you're up against. Just kind of annoying that early on here, it only knocks enemies on their asses, whereas the upgraded version you get later on outright kills them.

But still though, you are gonna use this a whole heap, from taking out standard enemies to flying drones and even gun turrets The final ability you get is Rushdown, which is where you get all charged up and super pissed off and can obliterate enemies with a quick flurry of punches And it is good, but it kinda drains your energy bar very quickly And I don't know, but I just never found it all that useful in comparison to stuff like the bullet time and the shield

The only time I think I ever really used it was during the endgame against these stupidly powerful mech suit things, and spamming this ability on these guys seems to be by far the best strategy to take them out. Along with absolutely abusing it during the final boss, which we'll get to soon enough. Either way though, you're really encouraged to use all of these and be as aggressive as possible, because killing an enemy using an ability is going to make them drop little pickups that give you a small boost to your health and energy.

making it quickly fall into a really good rhythm where you seamlessly find yourself swapping between weapons picking up objects and throwing them into enemies along with activating bullet time to quickly take out a group of bad guys and then catching all their bullets with your shield and launching them right back and i don't know like i might have a bad memory but i'm really struggling to think of any other shooter i've played in recent memory outside of maybe during the dark ages that just so effortlessly makes you feel like a total badass

A lot of the parkour moves like the wall running and the double jumping from the first game have been completely done away with here. Robots all you can do now is just climb up ledges. However, I think that's actually an improvement because it makes the combat feel far more focused and less about trying to make you utilize things like wall running just for the sake of it. And besides like it doesn't detract from the combat overall anyway where Sprawl zero just shits over anything we had in that first game.

And that's probably the biggest difference between this and the first sprawl I mean it always kind of felt to me like they wanted you to use the movement system and play the game the way they intended Whereas this one lets you play it the way you want to So it's less about bouncing around the room like a pinball and more about looking at the room and figuring out your ideal way to murder everyone that's in it And you can really tell too that they wanted you to feel overpowered and broken

I mean you're meant to be this super soldier that's been let off the leash this uncontrollable force of nature that no one can really tie down or stop and then about two thirds into the game you even get another buff to all of your abilities increasing your maximum health points but also your ability durations and decreasing the cooldown time with then the last third or so of the game just letting you run around at essentially max level

It is worth mentioning if the enemies in this aren't complete idiots I mean they're still gonna move around throw grenades and try to force your position and they are active enough that the combat doesn't feel like you're just shooting cardboard cutouts The thing is though is that you're just that much better than them that it doesn't really matter All up there's 11 chapters to play through and 12 if you count the prologue which will probably take you four or six hours to get through

And while four to six hours doesn't sound exactly massive, this is one of those games where I'd rather have five hours of concentrated violence than 25 hours of the same shit stretched out until I'm sick of it. And I know I've said this before, but I think people often overlook that simple, basic joy of a well-structured gaming experience that doesn't fucking waste your time. Anyway, things start off pretty basic with the first few chapters being quite simple in that regard.

Just in the sense that they're mostly linear as you're still coming to grips with all the mechanics and getting used to how everything works And it's not until about the fourth or so chapter in where it starts to open up a bit Having you go off in different directions now for multiple objectives This time where you've got to take out all these broadcast towers that are transmitting these propaganda messages Where it's almost like a domination match in a multiplayer shooter where you got to stand in the capture zone for a few seconds until it's over

you got three of these in total as well then you're able to choose to approach them in any order you want taking out enemies dynamically along the way too really giving it a whole sandbox feel with the final part of the level having you hold out in one spot defending it against waves and waves of incoming enemies after that they shift things up a bit with the next chapter having you move quickly through all these toxic gas clouds that slowly strip away your health reusing the same concept from the previous chapter where you can explore the environment in a far more non-linear fashion

as you again complete all these various objectives this time destroying the pipeline that's carrying the gas you come across these new phalanx enemies here as well these big dudes with an energy shield and a giant hammer which feels very similar to the gravity hammer in halo from the way that five holds it through to the way that sort of snaps onto nearby enemies for the kill anyway after that the next chapter does the same idea again

This time as you're trying to defuse a WMD that the rebels are supposedly planning on detonating, where they believe that the explosion's gonna kill hundreds of thousands of innocent people. To stop it, you've got to find and assassinate these three Imago Dei Triarchs who each have one of the arming keys. With these guys weirdly not seeming all that concerned that you've rocked up to kill them. In fact, they've got a fair bit to say there before you put them out of their misery.

Where their so-called keys instead being these holy relics that cause some kind of bizarre reaction and make Five's abilities go on the fritz Resulting in these really crappy combat sequences where your vision is all fucked to shit And you've got to take the enemies out without being able to use any of your abilities Not to mention without being able to see a goddamn thing. What's going on in there? What? That light! Oh, the red. Five! Five! Get back!

Yeah, this is easily one of the weakest parts of the game, and the only reason I can think of as to why they put this in is because, you know, maybe they thought they needed something to humble the player a bit. It is also worth mentioning that the game gets insanely challenging from this point on, with a noticeable difficulty spike and a real ramp up with the enemy count. This is where the plot does thicken though, because that bomb you are supposedly disarming ends up being armed by the Junter anyway, now being used by your superiors to apparently send a message to the rebels.

Bullshit, you know just in case it wasn't blindingly obvious by now that you're working for the bad guys I Won't spoil what happens though, but either way for the next level You're now completely unarmed and powered down and you spend most of this following chapter being chased by this new Colossus enemy Yeah, an enemy that people who played the demo are gonna instantly recognize Also completing these lame battery power cell puzzles while trying to not get squished by the guy

Ending in a section where I honestly got stuck for like 10 minutes because I just couldn't figure out what I was supposed to do Now in my defense, like this area does have all the hallmarks of a boss fight arena, right? So I assumed that I had to fight the guy Like I don't know, like maybe throw the power core things at him to do damage once his shield went down Or maybe I was supposed to power up one of these pylons and trick him into hitting it Only instead you have to go all the way back out again through another hole in the wall that this asshole's just made

Grab another one of those power core things so you can then use it to power this thing up and blast the guy with electricity like he's a gargantuan in Half-Life. I'm not a smart man. Oh yeah, and get used to picking these things up as well because this game absolutely loves these power core puzzles. Where you pick them up constantly and throw them around to like charge up a door or lower shield. Which is kind of annoying too because when you're holding an object you can't sprint or else you're going to instantly drop it.

And a lot of this stuff really just feels like blatant padding like an attempt to make some of these levels take longer than they otherwise would Also to consider during most of this chapter you've got none of your powers But you're still forced into combat where it really makes you realize just how much of the heavy lifting those mechanics are doing Oh, you're not to mention for all of this you've only got 50 health points given that five is supposed to be heavily wounded

Well, it sucks! At least when you do finally get your powers back, that sense of relief is palpable. And the next time you encounter those colossus things, you absolutely tear them in your shithole. I won't ruin where things go from this point or at the end of the game, because honestly, it is worth experiencing for yourself. But I will say though that it does do a good job of shaking things up a bit for those final few levels, with an entirely new area to explore and an entirely new enemy faction.

So for a game that runs about four to six hours, they've really made sure it's as varied as it could be My only real complaints about Sprawl zero come down to some of the enemies in the late game chapters Specifically how they behave and how it affects the difficulty Simply because these enemies you come up against later on, they're not smarter or more intelligent It's just that they have more hit points and better guns and also because you have to fight like three or four of them at once

and it's just kind of a shame that SPRAWL never really explores creative ways to tackle these enemies like maybe you could have used the gravity glove to strip away bits of their armor to expose them or I don't know stuff like that but instead it's really just about shooting them as quickly as possible before they melt you why won't you die even if you boss type enemies you do come up against can be beaten pretty easily by just grabbing projectiles and throwing them back or just you know shooting them over and over

I did mention it just before but it does bear repeating in how a lot of the chapters really do feel like they have blatant padding Kind of similar to Halo in a way where it'll often send you off in one direction to complete an objective Your main objective is to destroy the three distribution pipes in both locations Only to then just send you all the way back to where you started once you're done with new enemies of course along the way Then when you get back to that point you do the same thing only off in another direction and repeat this three or four times for the entire chapter

And some of the later levels are genuinely so repetitive and samey that I would have sworn I was just going around in circles If it wasn't for that handy objective marker helping me keep my direction We also really need to talk about the final boss in this because this thing is genuinely terrible Like it almost ruined the game for me For starters when you finally get up to it they give you a checkpoint before you fight the guy But not after you have to take out a few waves of enemies beforehand

and considering he's got a pretty tricky pattern you're gonna need to learn and you will die a bunch this means you have to re keep replaying that initial wave over and over until you learn what the pattern is and get it down pat which they could have simply just fixed by putting a fucking checkpoint before the main fight itself then once you figure out this pattern you'll see they essentially are just repeating the fight three times where you just have to repeat the same strategy in another identical looking arena

It's not like the boss fight adds in your moves or gets more challenging like, you know, actual boss phases would It's just the same fight repeated three times Which again, it kind of feels like a lazy way to pad the fight out I think it's also an issue because this is really the only proper boss fight you've got in the game Everything you had before this could be beaten pretty easily by just staying mobile But this boss right here has some highly damaging attacks and functions far more like a traditional boss fight does

And I'm not gonna lie man, but this fight almost made me not want to replay this thing. Almost. That's a damn shame. Luckily on a positive note, when you do beat this guy, you get to replay the game in New Game Plus mode, carrying over all your maxed out upgrades from the beginning. With this actually being worth doing too, because this New Game Plus mode has entirely new enemy placements, making it far more intense and challenging from the get-go, giving you a genuine incentive to replay the campaign. At least, you know, until you get up to that final boss.

Overall though, I still think SPRAWL zero is insanely good fun and definitely worth your time. And despite its niggling annoyances, the jump this thing has made from that first game is just insane. It's fast, it's violent, and it looks like that long lost console shooter from the early 2000s you never played. The movement's great, the guns hit hard, and once you get into that rhythm of turning enemies into a cloud of red mist, it's really hard to not have a good time.

I've been getting the vibe for the last couple of years that maybe we finally run out of 90 styled shooters to be nostalgic for and Sprawl zero is proof that we can start giving the early 2000s the same treatment And you know what if even half of them turn out like this well, I'm completely fine with that
